findings.reason: the author would either retarget the control at an interrupted-resume case or correct the case it claims to fail, so the node's gate can actually show the per-slice cache resume works.
findings.text: the second negative control ("Storing the cache only once, after the last slice, must fail the third case, because the second read would search again") cannot redden the third case at line 134 ("runs the same window twice and asserts that the second read issues no `-p` log"): for an uninterrupted read the cache is written once either way and the second read finds a complete entry, so it issues no `-p` log and the case passes under the mutation. The mutation in fact breaks a different property — resume of a read interrupted *between* slices (line 126) — which no done-when case exercises. As written the control demonstrates nothing about the case it names and leaves the mid-read resume guard unshown to fire.
